import re
import pytest
from target import url_basename

def old_url_basename(url):
    m = re.match(r'(?:https?:|)//[^/]+/(?:[^?#]+/)?([^/?#]+)/?(?:[?#]|$)', url)
    if not m:
        return u''
    return m.group(1)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        # simple paths
        "http://example.com/file.html",
        "https://example.com/path/to/file/",
        "http://example.com/file?query=1",
        "http://example.com/file#fragment",
        "http://example.com/path/file.html?query=1#frag",
        # root and missing path
        "http://example.com/",
        "http://example.com",
        "http://example.com?query=1",
        # non‑http scheme (should not match)
        "ftp://example.com/file",
        # double slash after domain
        "http://example.com//double/slash",
        # path segment containing a slash (the critical case)
        "http://example.com/a/b/c",
        # path segment containing query characters but no slash
        "http://example.com/a?b=c/d",
        # path with trailing slash and fragment
        "https://example.com/dir/subdir/#section",
        # path with multiple dots
        "https://example.com/dir.name/file.name.ext",
        # URL with port number
        "http://example.com:8080/path/file",
        # URL with user info
        "http://user:pass@example.com/path/file",
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_behaviour(url):
    assert url_basename(url) == old_url_basename(url)
